A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LearnArena study, and their main texts, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison. Table 5's missing content in v3 is confirmed visually, rather than being an extraction gap.

before.justification: v2 reports original learning experiments in Sections 4–7 and additional opponent-robustness, many-shot, and data-selection results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results across the three learning dimensions and LearnArena, including substantial appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Instructor interaction, concept injection, prior-experience selection, and the integrated LearnArena procedure remain unchanged. Appendix H's iterative data-selection procedure is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mathematical benchmarks, logic and planning tasks, competitive games, and four non-mathematical domains. The many-shot and noisy-data scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated models and learning-condition comparators remain unchanged. Appendix B still reports evaluation against Phi-4, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4o opponents; the missing Table 5 removes detailed scores without redefining the stated comparator set.

E3.justification: Model scales, clarification limits, experience-selection procedures, shot ranges, evaluation metrics, data partitions, and tuning settings are retained. The corrected averages are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: v3 omits Table 5's detailed evidence for robustness against a GPT-4o opponent, while retaining Appendix B's experimental description and aggregate rank correlations. Other sensitivity analyses, many-shot evaluations, data-selection analyses, and case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 repetitions with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting for in-context experiments in Appendix A.5. Match/run counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are otherwise unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 and Section 7 change GPT-4o's average from 0.75 to 0.77 and GPT-4o-mini's from 0.51 to 0.52, consistent with the unchanged per-game scores. v3 also omits Table 5's 24 win rates for six models against GPT-4o. These are corrections and removed result entries, not demonstrated performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3's task/context definitions and predictive mappings, together with Appendix D's formal distinction between instructional and experiential contexts, are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three-dimensional framework, LearnArena contribution, and claims about interaction, model scale, and few-shot versus many-shot learning.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning instructor quality, scale-dependent learning, many-shot degradation, and opponent robustness remain unchanged. Appendix G retains the same limitations concerning synthetic environments and real-world applicability.

D1.justification: Hardware, model identifiers, training hyperparameters, corpus sizes, prompts, and access information are retained. The existing code link moves from Appendix A.1 to the abstract; this does not establish newly available resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hu et al., Population-aligned persona generation for LLM-based social simulation, as reference 33 in Section 2's multitask-generalization citation group. Other cited works and the paper's research positioning remain unchanged after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: The code-availability sentence is lightly edited and moved into the abstract. The section organization and substantive narrative otherwise remain essentially unchanged, with pagination and line wrapping accounting for most apparent movement.

P2.justification: v3 reduces Table 5 to a bare label. Repositioned Figure 9 and Table 6 have overlapping captions on v3 page 29, and other floats shift with pagination. The plotted graphics themselves remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 2's averages improves numerical accuracy, but losing Table 5's robustness scores reduces verifiability, and the new Figure 9/Table 6 caption overlap harms readability. The correction is also incomplete: Appendix I.1 still reports GPT-4o's old 0.75 average. These localized losses outweigh the limited corrections and more prominent code link.
